accuracy.evidence: Definitions checked against CCSS ELA RL.6.2, RL.7.2, RL.8.2 and RI.6.2 to RI.8.2 (determine a theme or central idea, analyse its development over the text, objective summary) and the KS3 English programme of study. The topic/theme distinction and the three tests (full sentence, general, not a command) follow ReadWriteThink and common theme-statement guidance. The Mara story is original, so every beat label (introduces, develops, turning point, resolves, setting only) was checked against the text of that beat; m7's 'shaded streets measured several degrees cooler on hot days' matches US EPA heat-island guidance on tree shade.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips: a topic word given as theme (step 1 sort, p1, m1, challenge topicword), plot retold as theme (sort plot cards, m3, challenge plot), a moral written as a command (ladder options, p3, m6, challenge command), a theme tied to a named character (step 2 prediction, ladder 'specific', challenge specific), every vivid detail treated as a symbol (step 3 green-boat prediction, p5, challenge symbol and notext), judging theme from the opening only (m5, challenge firstline and title), and opinion in a summary (step 5, p4, m2, challenge opinion and judge).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagtheme works on one original story: sorting topic, theme and plot cards, sharpening weak theme statements by picking rewrites, placing five beats on a theme thread (introduces, develops, turning point, resolves, setting only), graphing the character's stance at four beats so the turning point is visible as a climb, and striking opinions from a summary. flagmoral finds a fable's moral, flaggist finds paragraph main ideas, flagtopic sorts key details for a topic; none traces an idea's development or graphs it. Gate similarity is under 30% to every lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner finds by sorting that a topic is a word while a theme is a sentence, sees named-character and command rewrites rejected with reasons, discovers that the vivid green-boat beat does not carry the theme, watches the graph stay flat until beat 4 and then climb, and is told why each factual summary line must stay. Each task's closing line states the rule just met.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions each with a tempting wrong option the lab then tests: 'Pride' as the theme (the sort files it under topic), 'Mara learns to accept help' as a theme (the ladder rejects the named-character rewrite), the green boat as developing the theme (the trace marks it setting only), beat 3 or 5 as the biggest change (the graph climbs first at beat 4), and that a summary should say if you liked it (those lines are struck).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with ten distinct wrong-answer messages: topic word, plot, opinion, judgement, 'not in the story', colour-as-symbol, command, named character, first line only and title only. Each names the slip and gives the fix, for example rewriting without names or turning a command into a statement.

readability.evidence: Learner kid text reads at FK grade 3.5 and adult at 5.9 (limits 6.5 and 9.5). Sentences are short and the terms are defined in place (topic, theme, turning point, objective summary). Canvas text uses short story beats of one or two sentences and bin labels of one or two words; the story is original so no copyright text is quoted.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate clean. Each kid paragraph adds one idea: topic versus theme, the three tests, how themes are built, tracing and objective summary. Items spread across topic and theme (p1, m1), statement quality (p3, m3, m6), development and turning points (p2, m5, m8), evidence choice (p5, m7), tracing across chapters (m4) and objectivity (p4, m2) with no repeated stems.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android light and 1200 px desktop dark screenshots of every step before and after Show me. At 360 px the card sits above three tall bins with labels centred in each, the five stage bins wrap into a 3 and 2 grid with readable labels and beat numbers, the graph keeps its wrapped row labels and four beat columns, and the six summary lines stack with strike-throughs visible; the tall 1.3 ratio stops text from shrinking below 10 px.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: Topic, Theme and Plot; each rewrite option; the five stage names; Beat N with each of the three levels; and Strike for each summary sentence. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after every action with the result in words. walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in light and dark themes on desktop and iPhone 13, with no console errors.
